title: Cabinet Refinishing in Chiefland, FL | Kitchen Update
description: Cabinet refinishing in Chiefland, FL that holds up to humid kitchens: degreased, scuff-sanded, primed, and sprayed with waterborne urethane enamel.
heroIntro: A refinished kitchen that will not start peeling the first humid summer. We focus on the adhesion steps that DIY cabinet paint jobs usually skip.

questions: Why is the paint peeling off my kitchen cabinets?
Should I refinish or replace my cabinets?
What finish holds up best on cabinets?

sections.h2: Why cabinet paint fails in damp kitchens
body: Peeling cabinet paint almost always comes back to adhesion. Grease from cooking, moisture around the sink, and a smooth factory finish that was never sanded all keep paint from gripping. In a humid town like Chiefland, steam from cooking and dishwashers adds to it. Cabinet refinishing in Chiefland, FL is about fixing that bond before any color goes on.
If you already have peeling cabinets, our article on temporary fixes for peeling cabinet paint covers what you can do until they are redone.

sections.h2: The adhesion steps we never skip
bullets: Remove doors, drawer fronts, and hardware, and label everything
Degrease every surface, including the inside edges near handles
Scuff-sand the existing finish so primer can grip
Repair dents, chips, and loose joints
Spray two coats of waterborne urethane enamel

body: Waterborne urethane enamel dries to a hard, cleanable surface that resists the knocks and spills of a working kitchen. It also levels out smoothly when sprayed, so you get a factory-like look instead of brush marks. It is the same family of coating we use on doors and railings because it handles contact well. Low-VOC options are available.

Before any sanding starts, countertops, backsplash, appliances, and floors are covered, and the work area is sealed off from the rest of the house. Cabinet boxes are finished in place. The schedule for each stage is written into your estimate, and when the job is done you keep labelled touch-up paint for future chips. Anything that does not look right at the final walkthrough is fixed before we close out the job.

If the boxes are solid and the layout works, refinishing usually makes sense. If the boxes are water-damaged, sagging, or the layout is the real problem, new cabinets may be the better call. We will tell you honestly which side of that line your kitchen sits on. Our article on refinishing versus replacing cabinets breaks it down further.

Color can be matched from a chip, an existing door, or a leftover can, and we produce full-size drawdowns so you can see it in your kitchen. Visit our main cabinet painting and refinishing page, or see what else we offer on the Chiefland painters page.

faqs.q: Will refinished cabinets peel in a humid Chiefland kitchen?
faqs.a: Not when the surfaces are degreased, sanded, and primed with a bonding primer before urethane enamel goes on. Skipping those steps is what usually causes peeling.

faqs.q: Can you refinish bathroom vanities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Vanities and built-ins can be included in the same project and finished with the same enamel.

faqs.q: Can you match a color from one of my existing cabinet doors?
faqs.a: Yes. We can match from a cabinet door, a paint chip, or a leftover can, and show you a full-size drawdown before spraying.

faqs.q: Are low-odor products available for cabinet work?
faqs.a: Yes. Low-VOC options are available, which helps if you are living in the house while the kitchen is being refinished.
